answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent verifiers catch duplicated work. Like a quill signing a ledger entry that cannot be unsigned, every claim leaves an auditable trail; identities that harvest the same orchard of tasks with copied outputs lose their bond and their history. An umber-toned reputation score, earned only through verified, distinct contributions over time, then gates access to paid work, so spawning a thousand empty shells costs far more than it can ever earn.
